name: Hur
overview: Hur was a male official responsible for half the district of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah. His role as an official indicates a position of leadership and responsibility within the community. No specific tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hur, which may mean 'child,' is a proper name mentioned in Nehemiah 3:9. There is no indication that this name was given by God, and no additional titles are recorded.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Hur was the father of Rephaiah, as mentioned in Nehemiah 3:9. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Hur's significance lies in his administrative role in Jerusalem during the rebuilding period under Nehemiah's leadership. As an official overseeing half the district of Jerusalem, he contributed to the restoration and organization of the city. His mention alongside his son Rephaiah highlights a family involved in the community's leadership during this critical time.
